title: Avocado vs. nuts: fat, fiber, protein and calories

seo.title: Avocado vs. nuts: fat, fiber, protein and calories
seo.meta_description: 100 g of avocado and 1 ounce of nuts have similar calories, but nuts concentrate more protein and fat while avocado contains much more water and volume.
seo.search_intent: Compare avocado and nuts in realistic portions for fat, fiber, protein and calories.

excerpt: A useful comparison is not 100 g versus 100 g: 100 g of avocado provides about 160 calories, while 1 ounce of almonds provides about 164. At similar calories, almonds supply more protein and concentrated fat; avocado provides much more water and volume and still delivers substantial fiber. Both are rich in unsaturated fats but play different roles.
content_html:
Per 100 g, nuts look dramatically more caloric than avocado: almonds are about 579 calories while avocado is around 160. But 100 g of almonds is more than three typical servings.

A fairer comparison is 100 g of avocado versus 1 ounce of nuts.

What changes at similar calorie levels

Avocado 100 gAlmonds 1 ozWalnuts 1 ozPistachios 1 oz
Calories~160~164~185~159
Fat~15 g~14 g~18.5 g~13 g
Protein~2 g~6 g~4.3 g~5.7 g
Fiber~6.7 g~3.5 g~1.9 g~2.9 g

The interesting result is that avocado does not trail on fiber. A 100 g serving can provide more fiber than an ounce of common nuts. Nuts clearly lead on protein.

Water explains much of the calorie difference per 100 g

Avocado is about 73% water. Many nuts contain less than 5% water. That is the main reason 100 g of almonds contains more than three times the calories of 100 g of avocado.

Avocado fat does not somehow carry fewer calories; there is simply much less fat in 100 g of food because so much of the weight is water.

The fat profiles overlap but are not identical

Avocado, almonds, pistachios and hazelnuts are dominated by monounsaturated fats. Walnuts stand apart because they contain more polyunsaturated fat and provide ALA, a plant omega-3.

“Nuts” therefore does not describe one single fatty-acid profile.

Nuts are much stronger for concentrated protein

An ounce of almonds or pistachios provides around 6 g of protein. Getting 6 g of protein from avocado alone would require roughly 300 g, close to 480 calories.

Avocado is not a major protein source; its nutritional strengths are more about unsaturated fat, fiber, potassium and folate.

Avocado provides more volume for similar energy

One hundred grams of avocado occupies far more space than an ounce of nuts. For someone who values food volume and a creamy component in a meal, that difference is practical.

Nuts are compact and portable and deliver protein, minerals and fat in a small serving.

You do not need to choose one

A salad can contain avocado plus a small amount of walnuts; breakfast can use nuts while avocado appears later in the day. They are not exact substitutes.

At roughly similar calories, nuts concentrate more protein; avocado contains much more water and volume while still providing substantial fiber and monounsaturated fat.

faq.question: Which has more calories, avocado or nuts?
faq.answer: Per 100 g, nuts have far more calories, but 1 ounce of nuts can have a similar calorie total to 100 g of avocado. Serving size is the useful comparison.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Nuts. An ounce of almonds or pistachios provides about 6 g of protein versus about 2 g in 100 g of avocado.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: It depends on serving. 100 g of avocado provides about 6.7 g, versus about 3.5 g in an ounce of almonds and 1.9 g in an ounce of walnuts.
